correctness.rationale: The proof derives \(S_\infty(A)=\log A+2\gamma+O(A^{-1})\) by explicit Riemann sums, subtracts the finite tail \(A/N+O(A/N^2+A^2/N^2)\), and solves the exact mean equation. Direct Riemann sums give \(A S_N\u0027(A)\to1\) and \(A\operatorname{Var}(R_N(A))\to1/2\). A split at indices below \(A^{2/3}\) establishes Lindeberg, and event inversion yields the Gaussian hitting-time law. The exact-root shift is \(c_\theta^2 N^{2\theta-1}+O(1+N^{3\theta-2})\), with threshold \(\theta=2/3\). The checker passed 72 finite/computational assertions, none of which substitutes for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: An actual critical-Zipf quorum reaches a random threshold at a nonstandard time scale; the Gaussian uncertainty and its coefficient were not supplied by the leading-order source. More importantly, the finite-N truncation contributes a positive centering term exceeding the fluctuation scale precisely for quorum thresholds above \(2/3\). This gives a sharp usability boundary for the natural published first-order centering; the exact-root law supplies the valid replacement without arbitrarily tuned parameters. It is a motivated second-order extension, not a textbook relabeling.
